| [ADR-054](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-054.md) v2 | Work is pushed to its pull request as it is made, and the pull request's CI repairs and lints it; contributors do not gate a push on running the record's checks locally | CLAUDE.md told contributors to run `luria repair`, `luria link --fix`, `luria index` and `luria lint` before every push. On a pull request the docs-check job already runs the repair, pushes it onto the branch, and lints the repaired tree, so the local run did the same work twice. At the record's present size it was also slow: on 2026-10-26 one local repair–link–lint pass ran past ten minutes, and work sat unpushed while it ran. At the owner's direction (2026-10-26), work is committed and pushed to its pull request as it is made. CI is the check, and a red check is read and fixed on the branch. `luria new` stays local, and a narrow local run is still allowed for diagnosing a red check. Rejected: keeping the local gate, a local lint only, and pushing straight to the default branch. | Active |
| [ADR-110](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-110.md) v2 | A postmortem is due when a schema change has been used, a batch of pull requests closes, a bulk filing lands, a decision is revised soon after landing, a process incident is fixed, or the owner asks; triggers count use and sessions, not calendar time, and a starting policy expected to be superseded | The owner asked on 2026-11-20 when to write a postmortem: not for every pull request, but perhaps for batches. Six triggers, measured in use and in working sessions because the record moves at about ten pull requests, one to five hundred entries and two decisions a day: a change to luria.yaml once about 20 entries use it or at the close of the first session that used it; a batch of five or more pull requests in a session, or any stack that had to be folded; a bulk filing of more than about 50 generated entries; a decision revised within the session it landed or the next; a process incident, once fixed; the owner's request. Not routine single filings that go green first time, nor the bot's repairs. The assistant checks the triggers when a batch closes and proposes; the owner decides. Short form for batches and incidents, the full form for schema changes. The owner expects this to be superseded: it is a starting policy, to be revised as postmortems show what is worth reviewing. Rejected: a postmortem per pull request; calendar intervals; leaving it to ad hoc request. | Proposed |
| [ADR-115](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-115.md) | A RETRO scheme holds retrospectives, reviews of how a change or a stretch of work went, including what went right; POSTMORTEM is kept for something that went wrong; the devlog holds notes taken during the work for the next retrospective; and the existing postmortems become retrospectives | The owner, 2026-11-21: "let's use it to document notes to revisit during the retrospective (we're currently calling this a POSTMORTEM, but that should be a rarer item and in response to something going wrong. we should probably keep the POSTMORTEM scheme, but add a RETROSPECTIVE scheme as well and convert our pre-existing postmortems to retros). A lot of stuff seems to be clicking right now, and we should document what seems to be going right." A new scheme RETRO; POSTMORTEM narrowed to incidents; [ADR-110](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-110.md)'s triggers divided between them; the devlog as the running notes; [POSTMORTEM-001](../../../record/postmortems.d/POSTMORTEM-001.md) to 003 converted. First application: the conversions, three devlog entries, a retrospective of the session of 2026-11-20 and 21, and a postmortem of its docs-check failure. | Proposed |
| [ADR-116](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-116.md) | Work merges into a staging branch through pull requests, and a Promote workflow merges staging into main nightly or on demand, concretizing a batch's temporary codes at once and merging main back; so units cite each other's codes without stacking, and the tooling fits how the work is done | The owner, 2026-11-21: stacked pull requests mean waiting for a CI run on each merge; "maybe a better solution would be to keep CI on main as it is, but have our regular work merge into an intermediate branch like staging branch, which we can then manually merge into main if we feel like it's ready … and add a nightly job to merge any dangling staged work into main", with the philosophy "to fit the tooling to accomodate the way we're doing the work rather than vice versa". Work branches are cut from staging and merge into it; a Promote workflow merges staging into main, runs docs-generate's repair, views and concretization on the batch, lints, and merges main back into staging. First application: the six-PR stack of 2026-11-20 and 21 folded into staging. | Proposed |
